_readme: This repository's own delivery-loop config: the plugin is built with the loop it ships. It has ONE trunk, `main`, so the base, hotfix base, production branch and release source are all `main`. `/devstride:release` is deliberately NOT used here: its model, a release source promoted to a separate production branch, does not fit a repository whose release is a version bump merged into `main` and tagged by the release-guard workflow. A release is cut with the repo-local `plugin-release` skill (`.claude/skills/plugin-release/`) instead. `mergePath` is owned by this repository and read by `scripts/check-merge-path.sh`, not by the plugin; `/devstride:doctor` may WARN that it does not recognise the key. Branch names, commit messages and pull-request bodies carry NO tracker item numbers, because this repository is public (AGENTS.md).

branchNaming.prefixSource: git user.name first name, lowercased; ask if empty or ambiguous

epicIntegrationBranches._readme: OFF in this repository. The loop learns which epic stories have landed on an integration branch by reading item numbers out of its merge subjects (build-item's next-unblocked rule), and this public repository forbids item numbers in git (scripts/check-public-hygiene.sh). So every story, epic member or one-off, ships through its own pull request into main, which is its own release. The remaining keys stay as written for the day the loop can record a landed story without a number.
epicIntegrationBranches.slugRule: epic title kebab-cased, lowercased, [a-z0-9-] only, execution-order bracket prefix stripped, truncated to ~6 words

mandatoryLenses.name: rule-loss-and-config-keys
mandatoryLenses.question: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Editing skills without losing rules': for every changed hunk, was an imperative dropped while the rationale that explained it survived; does a rationale that moved still hold where it now sits; does every config key a changed body cites still exist in a real config and does every key still have an instruction honouring it; and which claim of preservation rests only on a grep finding the words rather than on the rule still being true?

_repoLocalKeys_readme: Keys this repository's own tooling reads and the plugin does not: the plugin's config validator (doctor, setup check 0) stays silent about them instead of reporting them as unknown.

mergePath._readme: Repo-owned: read by scripts/check-merge-path.sh (run by the public-repo-guards workflow), never by the plugin. Matching is the plugin's anchored rule (skills/build-item/scripts/routing.py match). An epic branch reaches main only as a release, so the epic pattern admits a head only when the change bumps the version. No pattern carries an item number: this repository is public.
